st: Japan: between childhood and the future

sec.p: One step ahead. The financial/real-estate bubble of the '90s, the hikikomori phenomenon (hermits who impose a COVID-style lockdown on themselves), the demographic crisis: Japan seems to be sketching out the future of Western democracies.

Ignorant. Because of the geo-graphical distance (of their alphabet) I didn't know much about what, in the '70s - despite its defeat in the war - was the world's second-largest economy. Matt Alt comes to the rescue in Pop ポップ, with historical and cultural insights.
The series The Man in the High Castle imagines a Second World War without nuclear bombs, after which the East prevails and the streets of San Francisco are dotted with kanji (漢字).
